Background command completion

Opt-in command completion receipts resume gateway agents without Goal mode.

About 4 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Lifecycle and permissions 02 Verification

The gateway executor's interactive exec_command tool accepts notify_on_exit: true. An agent can select it when the user wants the result of a finite background command later. It works with every inference provider served by that executor, including Claude, and does not require Goal mode.

exec_command(cmd, notify_on_exit: true)
  → running session ID returned
  → agent may finish its first reply
  → process exits and its output settles
  → executor queues a runtime completion receipt
  → current turn settles
  → ordinary follow-up turn on the chat's current model and permissions

The option defaults to false. A command that finishes during its initial call returns its result normally and creates no completion turn. The receipt contains the session ID, original tool call ID and exit code. It is hidden runtime context, not a new user instruction or authorization. The agent can read retained output with write_stdin and verify the requested result. A process exiting successfully does not by itself prove that the user's entire objective is complete.

For existing tmux work, start a tracked command that waits for that specific job to finish and request notification on that command. Detaching a tmux process alone does not register it with the executor. Dev servers and other indefinite processes should keep the default unless the user wants an exit notification.

Lifecycle and permissions

The existing process watcher publishes at most one receipt after the initial tool call returns a running session and the final command event is emitted. Receipts use a bounded queue inside the existing executor. The input loop gives caller operations priority and starts a follow-up only through the existing automatic queued-turn admission. It waits while another turn is running or finishing, and does not interrupt another task. It does not poll inference.

Stopping the chat cancels its outstanding registrations, including while idle. Stopping a terminal, sending Ctrl-C, or clearing background terminals cancels the affected pending notifications. Reading a terminal's completed result also cancels a receipt that has not yet been delivered. A completion already admitted as a turn follows the usual turn interruption behavior.

Plan mode, an interrupted or failed agent, and host drain prevent an automatic start. Receipts do not change model selection, thread settings, sandbox policy, approvals, tool policy or task scope. Turn-only permission grants are not copied from the original command into the follow-up. Normal approval requests can still pause further work.

This is an executor capability, implemented by scripts/patches/gateway-background-completion.patch. The HTTP inference gateway does not execute tools or schedule turns. No LaunchAgent, cron job, app scheduler, provider-native tool execution or signed native-engine modification is added. API mode and other clients retain their own runtime's background-task behavior. Pending registrations live with the executor; they do not survive its shutdown or machine reboot. The command must run on a host that remains available.

Verification

The SDK build gate includes eight regressions for opt-in delivery, duplicate suppression, stop generations, runtime provenance, Plan mode, interruption and the finishing boundary. Run the real executor against isolated loopback mocks:

npm run build
node scripts/e2e-background-completion.mjs \
  --gateway /absolute/path/to/patched/gateway-codex \
  --control /absolute/path/to/unpatched/gateway-codex \
  --catalog /absolute/path/to/models_cache.json \
  --root /tmp/task-specific-background-evidence

The fixture checks a successful exit, a nonzero exit, default behavior, a short command, chat interruption, terminal cleanup, individual termination and an unpatched control. It also checks stop followed by an explicit user continuation, and a model change with updated sandbox and approval settings. Positive cases traverse both Responses and Anthropic Messages translation through the HTTP gateway and read the final command output. It uses private homes and synthetic model responses, creates no goals and sends no paid inference. A passing fixture proves executor delivery, not live provider behavior, desktop notifications, or a managed release rollout. A release must rebuild the SDK because the authenticated patch digest changes.

The 2026-11-02 development receipt records 33 passing SDK regressions and all 12 real-executor mock scenarios. The full Gateway test suite, build and typecheck passed. Independent review found and verified a fix for approval and conditional interruption paths. This was a development executable; no release was published or installed.
